title: Memphis Milano leaflet
lede: Christoph Radl’s 1983 Memphis leaflet: a catalogue grid of lamps under a row of labelled pattern swatches.
summary: Radl’s 1983 Memphis leaflet: labelled laminate and textile patterns over a grid of lamps.

creator.name: Christoph Radl (designer); Sottsass Associati (client); Memphis (publisher); Occhipinti (printer)

evidence.note: Downloaded the museum’s published image (500 × 364 px) from [the Stedelijk Museum](https://www.stedelijk.nl/en/collection/92956-christoph-radl-memphis-milano) to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The object has four parts; the image shows one side of one part. The record classes it as graphic design and does not say “leaflet”; that word is the catalogue’s description from the image and the 34.2 × 98.5 cm size.

styles.note: Official Memphis printed matter by the group’s graphic designer, showing its patterns and products together.

context: The Stedelijk lists Christoph Radl as designer, Sottsass Associati as client, Memphis as publisher, and Occhipinti as printer; 1983; 34.2 × 98.5 cm; four parts. [Stedelijk record](https://www.stedelijk.nl/en/collection/92956-christoph-radl-memphis-milano).

*Interni* says Radl began working with Ettore Sottsass in 1980, “designing the image of Memphis”, and later curated the 2022 Triennale exhibition “Memphis Again”. [Interni: Memphis Again](https://www.internimagazine.com/agenda/memphis-again/).
observed: A top row of pattern swatches is labelled by designer, name, and year, for example Nathalie Du Pasquier “Gabon” 1982 and Ettore Sottsass “Rete” and “Schizzo”.
The swatches include black-and-white nets and squiggles and bright color prints in pink, blue, yellow, and red.
A black band carries the “MEMPHIS MILANO” wordmark in blocky white letters.
Below, a grid of numbered photographs on black shows lamps by Bedin, Thun, Sottsass, De Lucchi, and others, each captioned with name and year.
interpretation: The leaflet treats patterns as products: laminates and textiles get the same captioned cells as lamps. For a website, the grid shows a way to lay out a Memphis catalogue without losing order.
borrow: Put pattern swatches in a strict captioned grid so the pattern is loud but the layout stays calm.
Use black cells behind product photographs so saturated objects stand out.
related: Pattern shown here: [Gabon](ref:du-pasquier-gabon-textile-1982). Wordmark study: [Radl’s logotype drawing](ref:radl-memphis-logotype-drawing-1982).

rights.statement: The Stedelijk links to a general copyright page; no open license is stated. No image is stored.
